summary: Ernst Gombrich worked in history, archaeology, and other fields, having studied at the University of Vienna. He held positions at the Warburg Institute as research assistant in 1936 and director from 1959 to 1976, and at the University of London (1956–1959).
Indologist Ernst Gustaf Ferdinand Olbers completed his Ph.D. at Lund University (1856–1862). He subsequently served as principal at Högre lärarinneseminariet from 1868 to 1879.

Indologist Ernst Haas studied at Bonn, Berlin (under Albrecht Weber), and Tübingen (Ph.D. under Rudolf von Roth). He was Keeper of Oriental Printed Books and Manuscripts at the British Museum from 1866 and Professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1875.
Ernst Haeckel studied at Frederick William University and Humboldt University of Berlin (1854–1857). He later served at the University of Jena from around 1861 to 1909.

Ernst Heinrich Meier worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Jena, Göttingen, and Tübingen (Ph.D.), also learning under Heinrich Ewald. At Tübingen, he served as Privatdozent (1841), ao. Professor of Semitic Languages (1848), and ordinary Professor (1856).

Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar Ernst Johann Eitel studied at the Maulbronn and Blaubeuren seminars and the University of Tübingen (M.A., Ph.D. 1871). In 1898, he served as a Lecturer in German at the University of Adelaide.

Ernst Kalinka, a scholar of history, archaeology, and other fields, studied at the University of Vienna (~1884–1889). He later held posts at Chernivtsi University (~1900–1903) and the University of Innsbruck (~1903–1935).

Scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies Ernst Kuhn studied at Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Heidelberg (1875–1877) and the University of Munich (1877–1917).

Ernst Leumann studied Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics at Geneva, Zurich, Berlin, and Leipzig (Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch). He served as professor at the University of Strasbourg (1884–1919) and honorary professor at the University of Freiburg (1919).

Linguist and Indologist Ernst Lewy studied at Breslau, Munich, Leipzig, and Berlin under Alfred Hillebrandt and Franz Nikolaus Finck. He was professor of Hungarian at Humboldt University (1925–1935) and later professor of linguistics at University College Dublin (1947).

Ernst Moritz Arndt worked in history, archaeology, and other fields, having studied at Greifswald and Jena. He held academic posts at the University of Greifswald (~1800–1811) and the University of Bonn (~1818–1860).
Linguist Ernst Moritz Ludwig Ettmüller studied at Leipzig and Jena, and under Bernhard Hirzel. He held positions at the University of Jena (~1831–1833) and the University of Zurich (~1833–1877).

Ernst Osiander worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at the Maulbronn and Blaubeuren seminars and the University of Tübingen (Dr. phil. under Rudolf von Roth). He served as Repetent at Maulbronn and Blaubeuren (~1852–1854) and the Tübinger Stift (1857–1860).

Ernst Otto August Heuman worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Uppsala University. He held positions with the Santal Mission, served as school principal and head of the Church of Sweden Mission, and became Bishop of the Tamil Evangelical Lutheran Church in 1921.

Ernst Philipp Ludwig Calmberg worked in Indology and other fields. He completed a Lic. theol. at the University of Jena (~1828–1830) and was a teacher at Gelehrtenschule des Johanneums starting in 1819.

Indologist and linguist Ernst Risch studied at Zurich (Ph.D. under Manu Leumann) and Munich (under Ferdinand Sommer). He taught at the University of Zurich from 1942, becoming ordinary Professor of Indo-European linguistics, Greek, Latin, and Sanskrit in 1959 until 1981.

Sinologist and Indologist Ernst Schierlitz earned his Ph.D. at the University of Munich under Lucian Scherman and Wilhelm Geiger. He worked at the Bavarian State Library, as librarian at Fu Jen Catholic University, and as director of the Deutschland-Institut.

Linguist Ernst Schwarz studied at the German University of Prague and the Deutsche wissenschaftliche Prüfungs-kommission in Prague. He later held a position at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1946–1963).

Ernst Schäfer worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology, studying at Göttingen and Berlin (Ph.D.), and under Erwin Stresemann. He was a Privatdozent at Munich (1942) and curator of natural history at the Lower Saxony State Museum (1960–1970).

Ernst Siecke, a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and religious studies, earned his Ph.D. at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He served as a schoolteacher and later professor at Lessing-Gymnasium (~1870–1914).
